**UK's largest banks back new domestic scheme to challenge Visa and Mastercard**

*A consortium of major UK banks is developing a domestic payment initiative that would use open banking rails to compete directly with the card networks on everyday transactions.*

The UK Payments Initiative, backed by several of the country's largest banks, aims to create a domestic alternative to Visa and Mastercard for retail payments. According to documents seen by The Banker, the scheme would initially route account-to-account payments at the point of sale, with the FCA describing its launch as a "concrete" development for UK payment competition.

The move is the most tangible response yet to longstanding regulatory pressure on card scheme fees in the UK. The PSR's recent proposal to mandate profit reporting by Visa and Mastercard, covered here last week, signalled that the regulator views scheme economics as insufficiently transparent. A bank-backed alternative, if it reaches scale, would give acquirers and merchants a credible negotiating counterweight.

Whether UKPI can overcome the distribution and acceptance challenges that have stalled similar initiatives elsewhere in Europe remains the central question. EPI's Wero in the eurozone is further along but still fighting for merchant adoption. The UK scheme's advantage may lie in having regulatory tailwinds and a domestic card market that is unusually concentrated.

*Sources: [UK's biggest banks back scheme to challenge Visa and Mastercard dominance](https://www.thebanker.com/content/2c2f7d00-f1e6-4854-bbf1-f90c9fe22c13) — The Banker*

**BIS cross-border tokenisation project proves wholesale settlement prototype**

*Project Agorá, involving multiple central banks and private sector participants, has built a working prototype demonstrating that tokenisation can address core inefficiencies in wholesale cross-border payments.*

The Bank for International Settlements has published results from Project Agorá, a multi-year initiative that brings together central banks and commercial players to test tokenised settlement of wholesale cross-border payments. The prototype demonstrates that unified ledger technology can compress settlement times and reduce the friction inherent in correspondent banking chains.

The project matters because it moves tokenisation from theoretical promise to demonstrated capability in the specific context where the pain is greatest: wholesale cross-border flows, where settlement still involves multiple intermediaries, time zones and messaging standards. Unlike retail-focused stablecoin experiments, Agorá operates within the institutional trust framework of central bank money.

For European payments infrastructure operators, the signal is that tokenised settlement is converging with existing regulatory and institutional structures rather than competing with them. The question is no longer whether tokenisation works technically, but how quickly it can be embedded into live clearing and settlement systems.

*Sources: [Tokenisation can improve wholesale cross-border payments - BIS project](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47819/tokenisation-can-improve-wholesale-cross-border-payments---bis-project) — Finextra*

**Bank of Finland frames European payment autonomy as a geopolitical imperative**

*A senior Bank of Finland official has argued that Europe's reliance on non-European payment infrastructure is a strategic vulnerability, calling for accelerated development of domestic payment capabilities.*

In a speech published this week, a Bank of Finland representative made an explicit case that European payment sovereignty is now a geopolitical necessity, not merely an industrial policy preference. The argument centres on the risk that dependence on infrastructure controlled outside Europe, whether card networks or messaging systems, creates leverage points that adversaries or even allies could exploit.

The speech places instant payments, the digital euro and domestic scheme initiatives such as EPI within a single strategic frame: building resilient European payment rails that cannot be disrupted by external actors. This framing has been implicit in EU policy for several years but is becoming more direct as the geopolitical environment hardens.

For payments executives, the practical implication is that regulatory and political pressure to adopt European alternatives to incumbent global networks is likely to intensify. The digital euro, SEPA instant payments mandates and support for domestic schemes are not separate policy threads but components of a single sovereignty agenda.

*Sources: [Geopolitical uncertainty and the future of payments](https://www.suomenpankki.fi/en/news-and-topical/speeches-and-interviews2/2026/geopolitical-uncertainty-and-the-future-of-payments/) — Suomen Pankki (Bank of Finland)*

stories.original:
**Plaid launches income verification for UK and European lenders**

*Plaid is extending its open banking infrastructure beyond payments and account aggregation into income verification, entering a segment dominated by legacy credit bureau processes.*

Plaid has launched an income verification product for the UK and European markets, allowing lenders to verify applicants' earnings directly from bank transaction data via open banking connections. The product targets a lending workflow that still commonly relies on payslips, employer letters or credit bureau estimates, all of which introduce delays and inaccuracies.

The move is notable less for the product itself, which several open banking providers already offer, than for what it signals about Plaid's European ambitions. Having launched its pay-by-bank product last week, Plaid is now building a multi-product presence across payments, data and credit decisioning in Europe. This positions it as a direct competitor to incumbents such as Experian and TransUnion in the affordability assessment layer.

For lenders, open banking-based income verification offers real-time data and reduced fraud risk compared to document-based processes. The competitive question is whether Plaid's brand and distribution, built primarily in the US, can displace providers with deeper existing relationships across European lending markets.

*Sources: [Plaid launches income verification tool in the UK and Europe](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/109960/plaid-launches-income-verification-tool-in-the-uk-and-europe) — Finextra*
